theme: World Records: Human Limits & Superlative Feats
title: World Records: Human Limits & Superlative Feats
description: A 60-question grand master assessment exploring Robert Wadlow, supercentenarians, Usain Bolt's top sprinting speed, Hafthor's 501kg deadlift, memory prodigies, 24-minute breath holds, Vesna Vulovic's fall survival, 3.13-second Rubik's cube solves, and cosmonaut space endurance.

questions.question: Who was the tallest verified human in recorded medical history, measured at an astonishing 272 cm (8 ft 11.1 in) before his death in 1940?
questions.explanation: Born in Alton, Illinois, Robert Wadlow's extraordinary height was caused by hypertrophy of his pituitary gland, which produced excessive human growth hormone.

questions.question: Who is the shortest verified adult person in medical history, measuring just 54.6 cm (21.5 inches) tall from Nepal?
questions.explanation: Chandra Bahadur Dangi lived in a remote village in Dang district, Nepal, officially measured by Guinness World Records in 2012.

questions.question: Which Turkish farmer holds the Guinness World Record as the tallest living man on Earth, standing at 251 cm (8 ft 2.8 in)?
questions.explanation: Sultan Kosen also holds the world record for the largest hands on a living person, measuring 28.5 cm (11.2 inches) from wrist to middle fingertip.

questions.question: Which Indian woman holds the Guinness World Record as the world's shortest living woman, measuring 62.8 cm (24.7 inches)?
questions.explanation: Jyoti Amge, who has a form of dwarfism called achondroplasia, is an actress who starred in American Horror Story: Freak Show.

questions.question: What endocrine gland located at the base of the human brain regulates growth hormone, whose overactivity causes gigantism and acromegaly?
questions.explanation: The anterior pituitary gland secretes somatotropin (growth hormone); non-cancerous adenoma tumors on the gland can trigger continuous linear bone growth.

questions.question: What was the exact standing height of Robert Wadlow, the tallest person in verified medical history, in centimeters?
questions.explanation: Robert Wadlow was measured at exactly 272.0 centimeters (8 feet 11.1 inches) on 27 June 1940, shortly before his death at age 22.

questions.question: Which French supercentenarian holds the undisputed Guinness World Record for the longest verified human lifespan in history, living 122 years and 164 days?
questions.explanation: Born in Arles in 1875, Jeanne Calment met Vincent van Gogh as a teenager, rode a bicycle until age 100, and lived independently until 110.

questions.question: Who was the oldest verified man in human history, living to 116 years and 54 days in Kyoto Prefecture, Japan?
questions.explanation: Born in 1897, Jiroemon Kimura attributed his longevity to eating small food portions (hara hachi bun me) and reading newspapers daily.

questions.question: What demographic term designates a person who has achieved the verified age of 110 years or older?
questions.explanation: While approximately one in 1,000 centenarians reaches 110, supercentenarians exhibit extraordinary biological resilience against cardiovascular disease and cancer.

questions.question: What demographic term coined by Dan Buettner identifies geographic regions such as Okinawa (Japan) and Sardinia (Italy) with exceptional concentrations of centenarians?
questions.explanation: Blue Zones share common lifestyle characteristics: plant-heavy diets, natural daily physical movement, strong community social ties, and purposeful living.

questions.question: Which American woman from Pennsylvania was the second oldest verified person in history, living 119 years and 97 days before passing in 1999?
questions.explanation: Sarah Knauss lived through seven American wars, the sinking of the Titanic, and the invention of automobiles, airplanes, and the Internet.

questions.question: How many full completed years did French supercentenarian Jeanne Calment live, setting the all-time verified human lifespan record?
questions.explanation: Jeanne Calment lived 122 completed years and 164 days from 21 February 1875 until her death on 4 August 1997.

questions.question: During his world-record 9.58-second 100-meter sprint in Berlin in 2009, what peak top speed in km/h did Jamaican sprinter Usain Bolt achieve?
questions.explanation: Usain Bolt hit his peak instantaneous velocity between the 60m and 80m marks, covering that 20-meter split in a blistering 1.61 seconds.

questions.question: Which American sprinter set the women's 100-meter world record of 10.49 seconds in Indianapolis in 1988, a mark that has stood for over three decades?
questions.explanation: Flo-Jo also set the women's 200-meter world record of 21.34 seconds at the 1988 Seoul Olympics, celebrated for her flamboyant one-legged running suits.

questions.question: In October 2019 in Vienna, who became the first human to run a marathon distance in under two hours (1 hour, 59 minutes, 40 seconds) in the INEOS 1:59 Challenge?
questions.explanation: Aided by rotating pace car lasers and alternating teams of world-class pacemakers, Kipchoge proved that no human is limited.

questions.question: Who holds the Guinness World Record for the fastest typing speed on a Dvorak keyboard, achieving peak speeds of 212 words per minute?
questions.explanation: Blackburn maintained a sustained typing speed of 150 wpm for 50 minutes and clocked peak bursts over 212 wpm in official tests.

questions.question: What is the average human visual reaction time to an unexpected visual stimulus under normal laboratory conditions?
questions.explanation: Auditory reaction times are even faster at roughly 140 to 160 milliseconds because sound signals reach the brain stem more directly than visual stimuli.

questions.question: What peak sprinting speed in kilometers per hour (rounded to the nearest whole integer) did Usain Bolt reach during his 100m world record?
questions.explanation: Usain Bolt reached an extraordinary peak speed of 44.72 km/h (27.78 mph) between the 60-meter and 80-meter marks in Berlin in 2009.

questions.question: Which Icelandic strongman and actor set the world record for the heaviest deadlift in history by lifting 501 kg (1,105 lbs) in May 2020?
questions.explanation: Hafthor The Mountain Bjornsson lifted the 501kg barbell at Thor's Power Gym in Reykjavik under official refereeing.

questions.question: Which British strongman became the first human in history to officially deadlift 500 kg (1,102 lbs) at the World Deadlift Championships in 2016?
questions.explanation: Eddie The Beast Hall's superhuman lift pushed blood pressure so high that he briefly lost consciousness immediately after dropping the bar.

questions.question: Which 19th-century French-Canadian strongman was renowned for incredible feats such as lifting 500 pounds with one finger and resisting two draft horses?
questions.explanation: Louis Cyr never suffered defeat in any strength contest and is considered by historians to be the strongest man of the 19th century.

questions.question: Which American weightlifting pioneer won Olympic gold in 1956 and was credited with a legendary back lift of 6,270 lbs (2,840 kg) from trestles?
questions.explanation: Paul Anderson's immense squatting strength helped establish powerlifting as an international competitive sport.

questions.question: Which Lithuanian strongman won the World's Strongest Man title four times and the Arnold Strongman Classic a record eight times?
questions.explanation: Big Z is widely regarded as one of the greatest overhead pressers and static strength athletes in strongman history.

questions.question: What is the official world record weight in kilograms lifted by Hafthor Bjornsson for the heaviest deadlift in history?
questions.explanation: Hafthor Bjornsson lifted exactly 501 kilograms (1,104.5 pounds) on 2 May 2020, surpassing Eddie Hall's 500kg record.

questions.question: Which Japanese mental memory master recited 100,000 decimal places of the mathematical constant Pi (π) from memory in 16 hours in 2006?
questions.explanation: Haraguchi used a custom mnemonic system associating Japanese syllables with numbers, reciting digits continuously with short hourly breaks.

questions.question: Which Indian mental calculation prodigy, known as The Human Computer, multiplied two randomly selected 13-digit numbers in 28 seconds at Imperial College London in 1980?
questions.explanation: Shakuntala Devi correctly multiplied 7,686,369,774,870 by 2,465,099,745,779 to produce the 26-digit product in under half a minute.

questions.question: What ancient mnemonic technique, also known as the Method of Loci, involves visualizing items to be remembered in specific architectural rooms?
questions.explanation: Attributed to the ancient Greek poet Simonides of Ceos, memory palaces allow mental athletes to memorize thousands of random digits and cards.

questions.question: How many playing cards are in a standard deck that world memory champions can memorize in under 15 seconds?
questions.explanation: Memory champions convert pairs of cards into vivid animated images, placing them in predetermined locations along a mental journey.

questions.question: Which German mental calculation champion holds multiple world records for calculating the calendar day of the week for arbitrary historical dates within milliseconds?
questions.explanation: Mental calendar calculators utilize modular arithmetic algorithms to instantly determine the weekday of any date spanning millions of years.

questions.question: What is the world record time in seconds for memorizing the exact sequence of a shuffled 52-card deck of cards?
questions.explanation: Elite memory grandmasters have achieved official competition records memorizing a complete 52-card deck in under 13 seconds (approx. 12.74s).

questions.question: Which Croatian freediver set the Guinness World Record for the longest voluntary breath hold (static apnea) underwater at 24 minutes and 37 seconds in 2021?
questions.explanation: Budimir Buda Sobat performed pre-oxygenation with pure oxygen for 30 minutes prior to immersion, raising awareness for autism.

questions.question: Which Dutch extreme athlete, known as The Iceman, has set dozens of world records for ice endurance and developed a specialized cold-exposure breathing method?
questions.explanation: Wim Hof demonstrated voluntary control over his autonomic nervous system and immune response during cold exposure trials at Radboud University.

questions.question: Which Canadian hero with an amputated right leg ran 5,373 kilometers over 143 days in 1980 in the Marathon of Hope to raise cancer research funds?
questions.explanation: Terry Fox ran a full marathon every single day across Canada until cancer spread to his lungs, inspiring annual Terry Fox Runs globally.

questions.question: Which American ultramarathoner famously ran 50 official marathons in 50 US states in 50 consecutive days in 2006?
questions.explanation: Dean Karnazes completed his 50-50-50 challenge by finishing the New York City Marathon on day 50, running a total of 1,310 miles.

questions.question: What British endurance swimmer completed long-distance swims in freezing waters across the North Pole and Antarctic without a wetsuit to advocate for ocean protection?
questions.explanation: Lewis Pugh was designated the UN Patron of the Oceans, training his body to raise his core temperature through anticipatory thermogenesis.

questions.question: What is the record time in full minutes for the longest voluntary breath hold underwater with oxygen pre-breathing set by Budimir Sobat?
questions.explanation: Budimir Sobat held his breath underwater for 24 minutes and 37 seconds in Sisak, Croatia, on 27 March 2021.

questions.question: Which Yugoslav flight attendant miraculously survived the highest fall without a parachute in history after her plane exploded at 10,160 meters in 1972?
questions.explanation: Vesna Vulovic was pinned by a food cart in the tail section of JAT Flight 367, which landed at a glancing angle on a snow-covered pine slope in Czechoslovakia.

questions.question: Which American computer scientist broke Baumgartner's skydiving altitude record in 2014 by jumping from a helium balloon at 41,419 meters (135,890 feet)?
questions.explanation: Eustace was suspended directly from the balloon without a capsule, wearing a custom spacesuit designed by Paragon Space Development Corporation.

questions.question: What cave in Abkhazia is recognized as the deepest known natural cave on Earth, explored to a depth of 2,212 meters (7,257 feet)?
questions.explanation: Speleologists take over a week of underground vertical rope ascents and descents to reach the subterranean terminal sump of Veryovkina Cave.

questions.question: Which American ocean explorer completed the Five Deeps Expedition in 2019, diving solo to the deepest point of all five oceans in the submersible Limiting Factor?
questions.explanation: Victor Vescovo reached a record depth of 10,928 meters in the Challenger Deep of the Mariana Trench, discovering new benthic species.

questions.question: What Swiss engineer and American naval lieutenant made the first crewed descent to the bottom of the Mariana Trench in the bathyscaphe Trieste in 1960?
questions.explanation: The bathyscaphe Trieste endured 1,000 atmospheres of crushing hydrostatic pressure during its historic dive to 10,911 meters on 23 January 1960.

questions.question: From what altitude in meters did flight attendant Vesna Vulovic fall and survive without a parachute in 1972?
questions.explanation: Vesna Vulovic survived a free fall of 10,160 meters (33,330 feet), holding the Guinness World Record for the highest fall survived without a parachute.

questions.question: Which American speedcuber set the official three-by-three Rubik's Cube single solve world record of 3.13 seconds in Long Beach, California in 2023?
questions.explanation: Max Park, who is on the autism spectrum, solved the three-by-three cube in 3.13 seconds at the Pride in Long Beach 2023 competition, holding dozens of world records.

questions.question: Which Australian speedcubing legend dominated competitive cubing for a decade, breaking over 120 official world records across various twisty puzzles?
questions.explanation: Zemdegs revolutionized lookahead technique and popularized the CFOP (Fridrich) method among millions of aspiring cubers worldwide.

questions.question: What is the name of the most popular three-by-three Rubik's Cube speedcubing method, consisting of Cross, First Two Layers (F2L), Orientation (OLL), and Permutation (PLL)?
questions.explanation: Developed by Jessica Fridrich and other cubers in the 1980s, the CFOP method solves the puzzle in four systematic, highly algorithmic steps.

questions.question: Which Hungarian architect and professor of architecture invented the world-famous mechanical twisty puzzle the Magic Cube (Rubik's Cube) in 1974?
questions.explanation: Erno Rubik created the three-by-three cube in Budapest as a 3D geometric teaching model for his students, selling over 500 million units worldwide.

questions.question: What competitive dexterity sport involves stacking twelve specially designed plastic cups in specific pyramid sequences against a digital timer?
questions.explanation: Sport stacking develops hand-eye coordination, bilateral dexterity, and ambidexterity, with world record cycle times under 5 seconds.

questions.question: What is the single solve world record in seconds for the three-by-three Rubik's Cube achieved by Max Park in 2023 (rounded to the nearest integer)?
questions.explanation: Max Park set the stunning world record of 3.13 seconds on 11 June 2023 in California, executing roughly 10 moves per second.

questions.question: Which Russian cosmonaut holds the all-time record for the longest continuous single spaceflight in human history, spending 437 consecutive days aboard the Mir space station?
questions.explanation: Polyakov, a physician, orbited Earth 7,075 times between January 1994 and March 1995 to study how the human body endures long-duration microgravity for Mars missions.

questions.question: Which American astronaut holds the record for the most cumulative days spent in space by any American or woman, totaling 675 days across multiple missions?
questions.explanation: Dr. Peggy Whitson was the first female commander of the International Space Station and performed 10 spacewalks.

questions.question: Which 1969 Apollo mission achieved the highest speed ever attained by a crewed vehicle, reaching 39,897 km/h (24,791 mph) during re-entry from the Moon?
questions.explanation: Crewed by Thomas Stafford, John Young, and Eugene Cernan, Apollo 10 served as the full dress rehearsal for the Apollo 11 lunar landing.

questions.question: What NASA robotic space probe launched in 1977 is the farthest human-made object from Earth, traveling in interstellar space over 24 billion kilometers away?
questions.explanation: Voyager 1 carries the Golden Record containing sounds and images of Earth, continuing to transmit scientific data back to NASA's Deep Space Network.

questions.question: Which Russian cosmonaut holds the world record for the most cumulative time spent in space by any human, surpassing 1,000 total days across five missions in 2024?
questions.explanation: Oleg Kononenko reached the unprecedented 1,000-day cumulative space milestone on 4 June 2024 aboard the International Space Station.

questions.question: How many continuous days did Russian cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov spend aboard the Mir space station on his record-setting 1994 to 1995 mission?
questions.explanation: Valeri Polyakov lived aboard Mir for 437 days, 17 hours, and 58 minutes, the longest continuous spaceflight in human history.

questions.question: Which legendary British explorer led the Transglobe Expedition (1979 to 1982), completing the first surface circumnavigation of the world along its polar axis?
questions.explanation: Sir Ranulph Fiennes and Charles Burton traveled 52,000 miles across land, sea, and ice, crossing both the South and North Poles.

questions.question: What is the highest commercial bungee jump in the world, allowing thrill-seekers to plunge 233 meters (764 feet) from a tower observation deck?
questions.explanation: Operated by AJ Hackett, the Macau Tower jump uses a specialized deceleration system and guide cables to control the 200 km/h freefall.

questions.question: Who was the managing director of the Guinness Brewery who conceived the idea for a definitive book of world records to settle pub arguments in 1951?
questions.explanation: Sir Hugh Beaver got into a debate while hunting about the fastest game bird in Europe (the golden plover), leading him to commission the McWhirter twins to compile the book.

questions.question: Which twin brothers compiled and edited the original Guinness Book of Records, published in Great Britain in 1955?
questions.explanation: The McWhirter twins possessed encyclopedic memories, fact-checking records for the popular BBC television show Record Breakers for decades.

questions.question: What is the deepest natural trench in the world, plunging to nearly 11,000 meters in the western Pacific Ocean?
questions.explanation: The Mariana Trench's deepest point, the Challenger Deep, exerts over 1,086 bars of pressure, comparable to having an elephant stand on your thumb.

questions.question: In what year CE was the first official edition of The Guinness Book of Records published in the United Kingdom?
questions.explanation: The first 198-page edition was bound on 27 August 1955, quickly topping British bestseller lists by Christmas.
